assessment.summary: This is a remarkably well-crafted orchestrator skill. The 9-step pipeline demonstrates strong structural integrity, exceptional token efficiency (1,210 tokens for SKILL.md), and a best-in-class progressive disclosure pattern using hub-and-spoke reference files. All 8 workflow integrity checks passed with zero issues, prompt craft scored 9.1/10, and the fail-fast ordering is optimal at every stage boundary. The primary concerns are external — a missing dependency agent (tjce-agent-release) that blocks the entire pipeline, and agent output path assumptions that need explicit integration contracts.

broken.issue: tjce-agent-release does not exist — the primary dependency for Steps 2-3 is missing from the repository. The pipeline is non-functional without it.

Agent output path mismatch — the orchestrator expects APF artifacts at {output_folder}/release/apf/ and manual artifacts at {output_folder}/release/manual/, but the existing agents may write to different base paths. check-deliverables.py will fail to find artifacts.

Stale verify-verdict.json accepted without scope validation — check-verify-status.py validates the verdict value but not which feature was verified. A developer who verifies Feature A and then ships Feature B will pass Step 1 with stale data.

opportunities.name: Incomplete External Integration Contracts
opportunities.root_cause: The skill assumes specific behaviors from agents and external systems that are not formally documented or validated within its own scope.
findings: tjce-agent-release referenced but does not exist (L5: AA-01, EG-01)
Agent output paths not contractually aligned with orchestrator expectations (L5: AA-02)
No documentation of expected agent headless interface within this skill (L4: agent contracts)
Agent exit code not checked alongside artifact existence in Step 2 (L5: EC-03)
Verify-verdict.json scope not correlated with ship scope (L5: EC-01)
YAML config parsed via regex instead of proper parser — fragile integration (L5: AA-07)

opportunities.name: Headless/CI Pipeline Gaps
opportunities.root_cause: Headless mode handles the run-until-gate scenario well but lacks mechanisms for programmatic gate resolution and machine-readable gate identification — making true CI/CD integration incomplete.
findings: No --gate-response flag for CI re-entry after human gates (L5: Headless)
Exit code 2 does not distinguish PML gate from deployment gate (L5: AA-06)
No timeout/watchdog for agent invocations in headless mode (L5: Headless)
No structured error output guaranteed on exit 1 (L5: Headless)
No notification/webhook mechanism when gates are reached (L5: missing patterns)

opportunities.name: State Management Fragility
opportunities.root_cause: ship-state.json is the sole persistence mechanism but lacks a formal schema, atomic writes, staleness detection, and concurrency protection.
findings: Schema never formally defined despite 8+ references across files (L5: EG-04)
No distinction between step started vs step completed in state (L5: Archetype E)
No staleness/expiry check on resume (L4: G3)
No concurrency protection for simultaneous invocations (L5: EC-02)
--continue does not validate that CLI args match stored state (L5: EC-05)

opportunities.name: Remaining Deterministic Work in Prompts
opportunities.root_cause: While the skill already delegates major deterministic tasks to 4 excellent scripts, several intermediate validation and infrastructure operations remain as LLM work, adding ~2,100-3,450 tokens of deterministic processing per full pipeline run.
findings: PML structural validation done by LLM instead of script — guards a non-negotiable rule (L6: Finding 1)
Ship state checkpoint management repeated 9+ times as LLM JSON construction (L6: Finding 3)
Release artifact intermediate check at Step 2 not scripted (L6: Finding 2)
Agent availability pre-flight check could be scripted (L6: Finding 4)

strengths.title: Exceptional structural integrity
strengths.detail: All 8 workflow integrity categories passed with zero issues. Reference files fully cover Steps 1-9 with no gaps, no overlaps, and correct progression directives forming a complete chain.

strengths.title: Best-in-class progressive disclosure
strengths.detail: The hub-and-spoke pattern with 3 semantically-grouped reference files is superior to per-step splitting. Each file is independently actionable within its phase, and the routing table in SKILL.md gives the LLM the full pipeline map before loading any detail.

strengths.title: Outstanding token efficiency
strengths.detail: 1,210 tokens for a 9-step orchestrator covering 3 agents, 4 scripts, 2 human gates, conditional branching, headless/interactive duality, error recovery, and state checkpointing. Zero waste patterns detected.

strengths.title: Optimal fail-fast ordering
strengths.detail: Every expensive operation is preceded by a cheaper validation gate. Every human gate is preceded by automated validation. The cheap verify-status check runs first, agent pre-flight runs before any delegation, and the deliverables checklist validates before the deployment gate.

strengths.title: Clean agent delegation boundaries
strengths.detail: The orchestrator never replicates agent logic. The explicit instruction 'Do not replicate this logic' in reference files is an exemplary boundary marker. Agents remain independently testable.

strengths.title: Comprehensive headless contract
strengths.detail: Exit codes (0/1/2) are consistently enforced across all reference files. Human gates correctly differentiate interactive vs. headless behavior. The --continue flag enables resume after gates.

strengths.title: Excellent script suite with full test coverage
strengths.detail: All 4 existing scripts follow a consistent contract (JSON output, exit code discipline, --output/--verbose/--format flags) and all have unit tests. The skill already delegates the heaviest deterministic operations to scripts.

strengths.title: Robust conditional logic propagation
strengths.detail: Task type and manual flag decisions flow consistently from detection (Step 1) through execution (Steps 5-6) to validation (Step 7) and summary (Step 9). The APF skip rule and manual conditional are enforced at every relevant point.

strengths.title: Well-designed human gates
strengths.detail: The AJUSTAR feedback loop at Step 4 captures feedback, re-invokes the agent with context, and returns to validation — preventing the 'stuck at gate' problem. Both gates are correctly non-automatable.

strengths.title: Direct, imperative language with zero anti-patterns
strengths.detail: No hedging, no meta-explanation, no identity preamble, no defensive padding. Inegociaveis section is genuinely load-bearing, not restating what the LLM would do anyway.

structure.summary: All 8 workflow integrity categories passed with zero issues. Frontmatter well-formed, all sections present and load-bearing, 3 reference files fully cover Steps 1-9, all 4 script references resolve with matching CLI signatures, output artifacts align, language is direct, config integration consistent, headless contract fully enforced, and cross-file logical consistency verified.

craft.summary: Exceptional prompt quality with zero waste patterns and best-in-class progressive disclosure. One compaction vulnerability (back-reference to SKILL.md Error Recovery in pre-check-and-release.md). Minor gaps in Overview script enumeration and intra-file progression markers.
issues: One compaction vulnerability: pre-check-and-release.md back-references SKILL.md Error Recovery section — should be inlined
Scripts not enumerated in Overview section
No micro-checkpoint between Steps 2 and 3 within the reference file

cohesion.summary: Stage flow is coherent with 1:1 mapping to all 5 manual phases. 9-step count justified by distinct responsibilities. Dependency graph correct with no cycles. Agent integration clean with low coupling.

gaps.description: No post-deployment rollback step if deployment fails after Step 8
No notification mechanism for headless gate transitions
No timeout or expiry for pending gates — stale state file from weeks ago could be resumed without warning

redundancies.description: Artifact existence validation in Steps 2/3/5/6 AND again in Step 7 — intentional defense-in-depth, not harmful

efficiency.summary: Fail-fast ordering is optimal at every stage boundary. Subagent delegation clean with no context leakage. Reference loading uses lazy three-stage pattern. Only 2 minor optimization opportunities totaling ~5-10 seconds of savings.

optimizations.description: Step 9 dual generate-ship-summary.py calls can be parallelized
Step 1 scripts could be chained with && using -o file output

journeys.summary: Smooth end-to-end experience with no friction points on the happy path.
Dead-ends at Step 1 if verify not run, with no onboarding message or vocabulary explanation.
friction_points: No introductory message explaining the pipeline
Error messages assume familiarity with process vocabulary (PML, APF, RDM)
No link to documentation or help command

journeys.summary: Blocked at agent preflight (tjce-agent-release missing). Even with agents present, two undocumented manual interventions required with no programmatic gate-response flag.
friction_points: Primary agent does not exist — pipeline non-functional
No way to pass gate decision programmatically
Must parse ship-state.json to determine which gate is pending

journeys.summary: Steps 5-6 correctly skipped, but two mandatory human gates create latency for emergency fixes. No expedited approval path.
friction_points: Two mandatory gates even for hotfixes
Full PML generation may be overkill for hotfixes

journeys.summary: Resume mechanism works but has ambiguity in state interpretation and no handling of partial artifacts.
friction_points: No distinction between step started and step completed in state
Partial artifacts from crashed step may confuse re-run
No integrity check on ship-state.json itself

scripts.existing_quality: Excellent — all scripts follow consistent contract with JSON output, exit code discipline, and unit tests

recommendations.action: Create tjce-agent-release or add a prominent 'DEPENDENCY NOT YET AVAILABLE' marker in SKILL.md with a tracking reference. The pipeline is non-functional without this agent.

Formalize agent output path integration contract. Document explicitly whether the orchestrator passes {output_folder}/release/ as the agent output path or agents must accept a custom directory. Add an 'Agent Contracts' section to SKILL.md.

Create scripts/validate-pml.py (~60 lines) that extracts H2/H3 sections, validates against expanded forbidden patterns (TODO, a definir, TBD, pendente, placeholder, empty body), returns JSON with per-section status. Invoke at Step 3 after agent produces PML.

Create scripts/manage-ship-state.py with init, update, read, resume-from subcommands. Enforce schema, atomic writes (write to .tmp then rename), two-phase state (running/completed), and CLI arg validation on resume.
Add scope validation to check-verify-status.py. Compare verify-verdict.json timestamp against most recent commit. If a feature identifier is available, validate it matches ship scope.

Inline the error handling rule in pre-check-and-release.md. Replace the cross-reference to SKILL.md Error Recovery with the actual rule: 'report with instructions to verify agent is installed and halt — exit 1.'
Add --gate-response flag for headless CI re-entry. Accept approved|ajustar|implantado|adiado with optional --rdm on --continue. Write pending_gate field to ship-state.json at exit 2.
Add AJUSTAR iteration limit with escalation. After 3 cycles, present escalation prompt: continue adjusting, edit PML manually, or abort pipeline. Write iteration count to ship-state.json.
Extend check-deliverables.py with --stage flag. When --stage 2 is passed, validate only the three release artifacts (CHANGELOG.md, deploy-checklist.md, rollback-plan.md).

Add post-deployment failure path. Either add ROLLBACK as a third decision option at Step 8, or explicitly document that post-deployment rollback execution is out-of-scope and refer to the rollback-plan.md artifact.
